'''Hervé Moulin''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSE|FBA}} (born 1 August 1950)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biographie de Hervé Moulin, Universitaire |url=https://www.whoswho.fr/biographie/herve-moulin-21824 |website=www.whoswho.fr |language=fr}}</ref> is a French mathematician who is the Donald J. Robertson Chair of Economics at the [[Adam Smith Business School]] at the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hervé Moulin's Website at the University of Glasgow|url=http://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/staff/hervemoulin/|website=University of Glasgow|access-date=27 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230912171331/https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/staff/hervemoulin/|archive-date=12 September 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> He is known for his research contributions in [[mathematical economics]], in particular in the fields of [[mechanism design]], [[social choice]], [[game theory]] and [[fair division]].<ref name="scw">{{cite journal|title=Hervé Moulin|journal=Social Choice and Welfare|date=2003|volume=20|issue=1|page=1|jstor=41106500|doi=10.1007/s003550200215|s2cid=189897557}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Salles|first1=Maurice|title=The Launching of 'Social Choice and Welfare' and the Creation of the 'Society for Social Choice and Welfare'|journal=Social Choice and Welfare|date=14 October 2005|volume=25|issue=2–3|pages=557–564|doi=10.1007/s00355-005-0018-6|s2cid=40849276|url=https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/560/}}</ref><ref name="The Moulin–Shenker Rule">{{cite journal|last1=Koster|first1=Maurice|title=The Moulin–Shenker Rule|journal=Social Choice and Welfare|date=22 November 2006|volume=29|issue=2|pages=271–293|doi=10.1007/s00355-006-0206-z|s2cid=35656861}}</ref>  He has written five books and over 100 peer-reviewed articles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Herve Moulin's publications on Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/scholar?hl=en&q=herve+moulin&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C5&as_sdtp=|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Herve Moulin's publications on IDEAS REPEC|url=https://ideas.repec.org/f/pmo321.html|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/staff/hervemoulin/#/biography,publications,researchinterests,grants,supervision,teaching,additionalinformation,books|title=University of Glasgow - Schools - Adam Smith Business School - Our staff - Prof Herve Moulin|website=www.gla.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-04-21}}</ref>

==Education and career ==

Moulin obtained his undergraduate degree from the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris in 1971<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/staff/hervemoulin/#/biography,publications,grants,supervision,teaching,additionalinformation,books|title=University of Glasgow - Schools - Adam Smith Business School - Our staff - Prof Herve Moulin|website=www.gla.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-04-21}}</ref> and his doctoral degree in Mathematics at the [[Paris Dauphine University|University of Paris-IX]] in 1975<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=81012|accessdate=30 April 2015}}</ref> with a thesis on zero-sum games, which was published in French at the Mémoires de la Société Mathématique de France<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moulin|first1=Herve|title=Prolongement des jeux à deux joueurs de somme nulle. Une théorie abstraite des duels|journal=Mémoires de la Société Mathématique de France|date=1976|volume=45|pages=5–111|doi=10.24033/msmf.180|url=https://eudml.org/doc/94718|access-date=30 April 2015|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bogomolnaia|first1=Anna|last2=Moulin|first2=Hervé|last3=Sandomirskiy|first3=Fedor|title=On the fair division of a random object|journal=Management Science|date=2022|volume=68|issue=2 |pages=809–1589|doi=10.1287/mnsc.2021.3973|doi-access=free|arxiv=1903.10361}}</ref> and in English in the Journal of Mathematical Analysis and its Applications.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moulin|first1=Hervé|title=Extensions of two person zero sum games|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|date=August 1976|volume=55|issue=2|pages=490–508|doi=10.1016/0022-247X(76)90178-5|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Moulin was the George A. Peterkin Professor of Economics at [[Rice University]] (from 1999 to 2013):,<ref name="scw" /> the James B. Duke Professor of Economics at [[Duke University]] (from 
1989 to 1999),<ref name="scw" /><ref>{{cite book|editor-last1=Coats|editor-first1=A.W. Bob|title=The Development of Economics in Western Europe since 1945|date=2000|publisher=Routledge|location=London|isbn=978-0-415-20291-6|pages=136–137|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wZKEAgAAQBAJ&q=herve+moulin+economist&pg=PA136|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref> the University Distinguished Professor at [[Virginia Tech]] (from 
1987 to 1989),<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Virginia Tech's Distinguished Professors|url=https://www.unirel.vt.edu/history/faculty_staff/distinguished_professors.html|website=Virginia Tech Website|access-date=30 April 2015|archive-date=13 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150513194051/http://www.unirel.vt.edu/history/faculty_staff/distinguished_professors.html}}</ref> and Academic Supervisor at [[Higher School of Economics]] in St. Petersburg, Russia (from 
2015 to 2022).<ref>{{cite web|title=Staff - Hervé Moulin - HSE University|url=https://www.hse.ru/en/org/persons/168405491|website=Higher School of Economics Website|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921204052/https://www.hse.ru/en/org/persons/168405491 |access-date=28 March 2023|archive-date=2021-09-21 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bogomolnaia|first1=Anna|last2=Moulin|first2=Hervé|last3=Sandomirskiy|first3=Fedor|title=On the fair division of a random object|journal=Management Science|date=2022|volume=68|issue=2 |pages=809–1589|doi=10.1287/mnsc.2021.3973|doi-access=free|arxiv=1903.10361}}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[Econometric Society]] since 1983,<ref>{{cite web|title=The Econometric Society Fellows by January of 2015|url=https://www.econometricsociety.org/society/organization-and-governance/fellows|publisher=The Econometric Society|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref> and the president of the Game Theory Society for the term 2016 - 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/staff/hervemoulin/#/biography,publications,researchinterests,grants,supervision,teaching,additionalinformation,books|title=University of Glasgow - Hervé Moulin|publisher=The Game Theory Society|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gametheorysociety.org/|title=Elections of GTS Officers 2016|date=31 August 2016|website=Game Theory Society Webpage|access-date=31 August 2016}}</ref> He also served as president of the Society for Social Choice and Welfare for the period of 1998 to 1999.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Society for Social Choice and Welfare Current and Past Presidents|url=http://www.unicaen.fr/recherche/mrsh/scw/council|publisher=The Society for Social Choice and Welfare|access-date=30 April 2015|archive-date=12 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612005951/http://www.unicaen.fr/recherche/mrsh/scw/council}}</ref> He became a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=2015 Elected Fellows|url=http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/1168_2015ElectedFellows.html|website=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref>

== Research ==
On 1979, Moulin published a seminal paper in [[Econometrica]] introducing the notion of dominance solvable games.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moulin|first1=Herve|title=Dominance Solvable Voting Schemes|journal=Econometrica|date=November 1979|volume=47|issue=6|pages=1337–1351|doi=10.2307/1914004|jstor=1914004}}</ref> Dominance solvability is a solution concept for games which is based on an iterated procedure of deletion of dominated strategies by all participants. Dominance solvability is a stronger concept than [[Nash equilibrium]] because it does not require ex-ante coordination. Its only requirement is iterated common knowledge of rationality. His work on this concept was mentioned in [[Eric Maskin]]'s Nobel Prize Lecture.<ref>{{cite web | title=Eric Maskin's Nobel Prize Lecture |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/economic-sciences/laureates/2007/maskin-lecture.html| access-date=April 29, 2015}}</ref>

One year later he proved an interesting result concerning the famous [[Gibbard–Satterthwaite theorem|Gibbard-Satterthwaite Theorem]],<ref>{{cite web|last1=Laffont|first1=Jean-Jacques|title=William Vickrey: A Pioneer in the Economics of Incentives|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/economic-sciences/laureates/1996/vickrey-lecture_laffont.pdf|website=The Official Website of the Nobel Prize|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref> which states that any voting procedure on the universal domain of preferences whose range contains more than two alternatives is either dictatorial or manipulable. Moulin proved that it is possible to define non-dictatorial and non-manipulable social choice functions in the restricted domain of single-peaked preferences, i.e. those in which there is a unique best option, and other options are better as they are closer to the favorite one. Moreover, he provided a characterization of such rules.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moulin |first1=Herve |title=On Strategy-proofness and Single Peakedness |journal=Public Choice |date=1980 |volume=35 |issue=4 |pages=437–455 |doi=10.1007/BF00128122 |s2cid=154508892 }}</ref> This paper inspired a whole literature on achieving strategy-proofness and fairness (even in a weak form as non-dictatorial schemes) on restricted domains of preferences.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Ed. by Kenneth J. Arrow|title=Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare|date=2003|publisher=Elsevier|location=Amsterdam|isbn=978-0-444-50894-2|pages=760–780|edition=1 |display-authors=etal}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Ed. by Robert J. Aumann|title=Handbook of Game Theory|date=2006|publisher=North-Holland|location=Amsterdam|isbn=978-0-444-89427-4|edition=3 impr.|display-authors=etal}}</ref>

Moulin is also known for his seminal work in [[cost sharing]]<ref name="The Moulin–Shenker Rule"/><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Roughgarden|first1=Tim|last2=Sundararajan|first2=Mukund|title=Quantifying Inefficiency in Cost-sharing Mechanisms|journal=Journal of the ACM|date=1 June 2009|volume=56|issue=4|pages=1–33|doi=10.1145/1538902.1538907|s2cid=68933}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Brenner|first1=Janina|last2=Schäfer|first2=Guido|title=Group-strategyproof Cost Sharing mechanisms for Makespan and other Scheduling Problems|journal=Theoretical Computer Science|date=July 2008|volume=401|issue=1–3|pages=96–106|doi=10.1016/j.tcs.2008.03.025|doi-access=free}}</ref> and assignment problems.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Abdulkadiroğlu|first1=Atila|last2=Sönmez|first2=Tayfun|title=Ordinal Efficiency and Dominated Sets of Assignments|journal=Journal of Economic Theory|date=September 2003|volume=112|issue=1|pages=157–172|doi=10.1016/S0022-0531(03)00091-7|hdl=10161/1940|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Aziz|first1=Haris|last2=Brandt|first2=Felix|last3=Brill|first3=Markus|last4=Mestre|first4=Julián|title=Computational aspects of random serial dictatorship|journal=ACM SIGecom Exchanges|date=28 January 2015|volume=13|issue=2|pages=26–30|doi=10.1145/2728732.2728735|s2cid=6352668}}</ref> In particular, jointly with [[Anna Bogomolnaia]], he proposed the [[probabilistic-serial procedure]] as a solution to the [[fair random assignment]] problem, which consists of dividing several goods among a number of persons. Probabilistic serial allows each person to "eat" her favorite shares, hence defining a probabilistic outcome. It always produces an outcome which is unambiguously efficient ex-ante, and thus has a strong claim over the popular [[random priority item allocation|random priority]]. The paper was published in 2001 in the ''[[Journal of Economic Theory]]''. By summer of 2016, the article had 395 citations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=7kaIUXoAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra|title=Anna Bogomolnaia}}</ref>

He has been credited as the first proposer of the famous beauty contest game, also known as the guessing game, which shows that players fail to anticipate strategic behavior from other players. Experiments testing the equilibrium prediction of this game started the field of experimental economics.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rosemarie|first=Nagel|author-link=Rosemarie Nagel|year=2016|title=Inspired and inspiring: Hervé Moulin and the discovery of the beauty contest game|journal=Mathematical Social Sciences|volume=90|pages=191–207|doi=10.1016/j.mathsocsci.2016.09.001|url=https://econ-papers.upf.edu/papers/1539.pdf}}</ref>

Moulin's research has been supported in part by seven grants from the US [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rice economist receives NSF grant|url=http://socialsciences.rice.edu/Content.aspx?id=2147483992&blogid=90|website=Rice University|access-date=30 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924211819/http://socialsciences.rice.edu/Content.aspx?id=2147483992&blogid=90|archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> He collaborates as an adviser with the fair division website Spliddit, created by [[Ariel Procaccia]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spliddit: The Team|url=http://www.spliddit.org/about|website=Spliddit Website|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref> On the occasion of his 65th birthday, the [[Paris School of Economics]] and the [[Aix-Marseille University]] organised a conference in his honor, with [[Peyton Young]], William Thomson, Salvador Barbera, and Moulin himself among the speakers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Conférence en l'honneur d'Hervé Moulin|url=http://www.amse-aixmarseille.fr/evenement/conference-en-lhonneur-dherve-moulin|access-date=25 October 2015|archive-date=6 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106121741/https://www.amse-aixmarseille.fr/evenement/conference-en-lhonneur-dherve-moulin}}</ref> In July 2018 Moulin was elected Fellow of the [[British Academy]] (FBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britac.ac.uk/news/record-number-academics-elected-british-academy|title=Record number of academics elected to British Academy {{!}} British Academy|website=British Academy|language=en|access-date=2018-07-22}}</ref>

==Bibliography==

Moulin has published work jointly with [[Matthew O. Jackson]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jackson|first1=Matthew|last2=Moulin|first2=Hervé|title=Implementing a Public Project and Distributing its Cost|journal=Journal of Economic Theory|date=June 1992|volume=57|issue=1|pages=125–140|doi=10.1016/S0022-0531(05)80044-4}}</ref> [[Scott Shenker]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moulin|first1=Hervé|last2=Shenker|first2=Scott|title=Serial Cost Sharing|journal=Econometrica|date=September 1992|volume=60|issue=5|pages= 1009–1037|doi=10.2307/2951537|jstor=2951537}}</ref> and [[Anna Bogomolnaia]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bogomolnaia|first1=Anna|author1-link= Anna Bogomolnaia |last2=Moulin|first2=Hervé|title=A New Solution to the Random Assignment Problem|journal=Journal of Economic Theory|date=October 2001|volume=100|issue=2|pages=295–328|doi=10.1006/jeth.2000.2710}}</ref> among many other academics.
